content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The TIME_FORMAT() function formats a time by a specified format.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT TIME_FORMAT("19:30:10", "%H %i %s");

---

TIME_FORMAT(
time
,
format
)

---

SELECT TIME_FORMAT("19:30:10", "%h %i %s %p");

---

SELECT TIME_FORMAT("19:30:10", "%r");

---

SELECT TIME_FORMAT("19:30:10", "%T");
```

## Tutorials

The TIME_TO_SEC() function converts a time value into seconds.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT TIME_TO_SEC("19:30:10");

---

TIME_TO_SEC(
time
)

---

SELECT TIME_TO_SEC("00:00:05");

---

SELECT TIME_TO_SEC("03:30:00.999999");

---

SELECT TIME_TO_SEC("-03:30:00");
```

## Tutorials

The TIMEDIFF() function returns the difference between two 
time/datetime expressions.

Note:time1andtime2should be in the 
same format, and the calculation istime1-time2.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT TIMEDIFF("13:10:11", "13:10:10");

---

TIMEDIFF(
time1
,
time2
)

---

SELECT TIMEDIFF("2017-06-25 13:10:11", "2017-06-15 13:10:10");
```

## Tutorials

The TIMESTAMP() function returns a datetime value based on a date or datetime value.

Note:If there are specified two arguments with this 
function, it first adds the second argument to the first, and then returns a 
datetime value.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT TIMESTAMP("2017-07-23",  "13:10:11");

---

TIMESTAMP(
expression
,
time
)

---

SELECT TIMESTAMP("2017-07-23");
```

## Tutorials

The TO_DAYS() function returns the number of days between a date and year 0 
(date "0000-00-00").

The TO_DAYS() function can be used only with dates within the Gregorian 
calendar.

Note:This function is the opposite of theFROM_DAYS()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT TO_DAYS("2017-06-20");

---

TO_DAYS(
date
)

---

SELECT TO_DAYS("2017-06-20 09:34:00");
```
